title: POLICY & PROCEDURE PLAN FOR FIRE AND NON-FIRE EMERGENCIES
html:
POLICY & PROCEDURE

PLAN FOR FIRE AND NON-FIRE EMERGENCIES

  • PURPOSE:
    • To provide guidelines & document the plan for fire and non-fire emergencies from within the hospital.
  • SCOPE:
    • Hospital – wide
  • RESPONSIBILTY:
    • Maintenance Department
  • ABBREVIATION:
    • NABH: National Accreditation Board For Hospitals and Healthcare providers
    • FMS: Facility Management and Safety
    • CA: Corrective Action
    • PA: Preventive Action
  • DEFINITION: Nil.
  • REFERENCE:
    • NABH: Pre Accreditation Entry Level Standards for Hospitals, First Edition, April 034.
    • FMS.4. The organization has plans for fire and non-fire emergencies within the facilities.. (OE a – d).
  • POLICY:
    • The hospital has a firefighting team drawn from the hospital staff.
    • They are given the necessary training to use firefighting equipment and given instructions on how to react to ‘in house fire accidents’.
    • When the CODE RED is announced by the general alarm bell or Public Announcement system, the fire-fighting team will rush to the site of fire accident and on reaching the site will coordinate their action to extinguish the fire by the time the informed fire force arrives at the site.
    • The fire-fighting team will conduct the safe and organized evacuation of the people from the site in an orderly manner and without creating panic or confusion.
    • The fire drills shall be conducted twice a year.
    • There is an established maintenance plan for all fire-fighting equipment.
  • PROCEDURE:
    • This hospital has provisions and facilities to combat any fire emergencies. All the floors of the hospital is provided with automatic water sprinklers systems controlled electronically and have access to firefighting equipment and water hoses at vantage points. High power pumps are installed to pump water in case of fire hazard.
    • The hospital has marked fire exits strategically located. The emergency exit routes are marked. Each patient room and common passages have marked directions of the exit routes to be used in the case of fire and other emergencies. Fire extinguishers and other firefighting equipment’s are provided in high risk areas like the medical records room, pharmacy, store etc.
    • Besides the members of the ‘Fire Fighting Team’ other staffs both medical and non-medical are trained to react and combat in such emergencies, with the priority to protect the patients and valuable hospital equipment’s and assets.
    • The Fire Fighting Team organizes mock fire and emergency drills twice a year with the help and guidance from the local fire fighting force. All staff takes part the drill which gives emphasis of safe evacuation of the patients and occupants in the affected areas or hospital in general, as the firefighting and containment activity is under progress.
    • Hospital Fire Fighting Team:
      • During Daytime [8:00 am to 5:00 pm]:
      • During Night Time [5:00 pm to 8:00 am]:
    • Fire Safety Protocol:
      • Fire Preventive Measures:
        • Fire risk areas in the Hospital are identified as given below:- Generator Room; Substation; Medical Gas storage room and medical record room.
        • At these places, First Aid fire appliances are provided.
        • In case of any fire incident the following action is to be taken:- Try to put it off; Shout for help in case not being able to put it off; If it is an electrical fire, inform to reception or cutting off the power supply.
        • In case of fire in the hospital building and surrounding areas following action is to be taken:- Immediately try to put it off; If not extinguished ,shout to help; Switch off the electrical supply; Inform to reception Shift the patient to safer places. If fire has not been extinguished, without panic direct the patients to safer locations through fire escape route.
        • Use fire escape route for going out of the hospital building (Fire /Emergency escape route is drawn and displayed at all floors important locations for information of patient and staff).
    • Fire Fighting Instructions:
      • The fire-fighting is an emergency requirement and this is called as CODE RED in this hospital it will be alerted through Public Announcement system/bell/fire alarm.
      • Fire accidents may occur any time. If these fire accidents are not attended immediately it can cause loss to life and property. In case a fire incident is noticed at this hospital area, the following action is to be taken:-
        • Try to put off electric equipment.
        • Shout for help in case assistance is required. If unable to put off inform to reception [Security Supervisor] about the type of fire and location of fire. Security Supervisor will activate “Code Red” signal and assemble the firefighting team consisting of the following personnel on duty at this hospital. Security Supervisor will inform all the above personnel and reach the fire site without delay. If it is an electrical fire the electric supply should be switched off by informing duty electrician. Water will be used if it is confirmed as solid fire. If evacuation is required, the evacuation plan is to be activated. The Security Supervisor will maintain a record of the fire accident by noting the date, time of call and time of dousing the fire and loss of life or property if any. If the fire is not controllable the matter to be informed to civil fire station for immediate help while informing give type of fire and correct location of fire. The firefighting team shall reach to the place of fire without delay and organize firefighting after getting this warning of “ Code Red ”
    • Fire Prevention Points:
      • Do not store inflammable materials like petrol, LPG, in the hospital building and rooms.
      • Do not use kerosene stove, burners, gas stoves in the hospital rooms and department.
      • The spirit lamp used in the laboratory should be placed in a safe place and put off after use.
      • Do not use the candles / oil lamp to light the rooms department.
      • Do not use the unauthorized electrical appliance in this hospital rooms and department.
      • Do not store the loose papers files and old record in card board boxes.
      • The old record room should be properly ventilated and electrical line protected against the fire.
      • All important departments will be provided with the first aid fire appliance.
      • Do not leave the remains of used match stick, candles or cloth pieces etc in the floor area.
      • Extinguish and throw these items in dust bin only.
      • Put off electrical supply to the rooms in case any spark is noticed and inform duty electrician.
      • While refueling the diesel tank of generator take fire precautions and do not bring any lighted material near to the refueling point.
      • Put off all light fans and electrical equipment and remove the equipment connection from the plug while locking the room after the work.
    • Emergency Evacuation Plan /Emergency Exit: Ground Floor Occupants: In the event of fire or other emergencies which warrant the evacuation of patients and duty personnel, please be guided by the following evacuation plan:
      • Alert all inmates one by one and room by room of the emergency situation without causing undue panic and commotion while informing the matter.
      • Evacuate all the patients first with the help of stretcher, trolleys or by the wheeled cots.
      • The medical documents of the particular patient should be sent along as well.
      • The only route to be used for evacuation of such patients should be the hospital Staircase.
      • The lifts should not be used in such situations.
      • Ambulatory of semi-ambulatory patients should be evacuated one by one using wheel chairs.
      • The patient’s medical documents should be sent along.
      • Evacuation should be done in an orderly manner without causing confusion or panic.
      • These patients will occupy the vacant beds on the other floors except the affected area.
      • Casualty observation beds or crisis management beds on the ground floor shall also be used.
      • The duty personnel will leave the emergency affected floor last after ensuring that all the patients, their personal belongings and medical documents are safely evacuated.
    • Fire Fighting Appliances Within The Hospital (Refer Annexure 1 And 2):
      • First aid appliances:-Foam extinguisher, powder compound extinguisher, CO2 gas extinguisher.
      • Major fire appliances.
      • Water facilities within the corridors
    • Fire Fighting Training:
      • The Fire Fighting Team organizes mock fire and emergency drills twice a year with the help and guidance from the local fire fighting force.
      • All staff takes part the drill which gives emphasis of safe evacuation of the patients and occupants in the affected areas or hospital in general, as the fire-fighting and containment activity is under progress.


Annexure 1: FIRE PROCEDURE

PULL-CALL-FIGHT – EVACUATE

  • REMOVE ANYONE IN DANGER area
  • PULL ALARM
  • CALL the hospital fire number and give them exact location, stating building, floor and room number
  • FIGHT FIRE. Isolate area, close nearby doors and windows. If safe to do so, shutoff electrical appliances and oxygen. Turn off all lab experiments. Including all gases in the general area of the fire. Attempt to extinguish or control spread of fire with extinguisher, hose, wet blankest, etc.
  • EVACUATE - To the safest stairwell. Evacuation on patient floors only will be determined by the Nursing Superintend

KNOW Location of fire alarms on your floor

KNOW “Fire Alarm Code” for your area (found at the pull-box station)

KNOW Location and correct operation of fire extinguishing equipment

The term "Code Red" is used within the hospital in place of the word "Fire".

Do not use elevators during a "Code Red".

NON FIRE EMMERGENCY:

“Any occurrence that causes damage, ecological disruption, loss of human life, deterioration of health and health services, on a scale sufficient to warrant an extraordinary response from outside the community” (WHO).

A disaster is an extreme disruption of the functioning of a society that causes widespread human, material, or environmental losses that exceed the ability of the affected society to cope using only its own resources. Events such as earthquakes, floods, and cyclones, by themselves, are not considered disasters. Rather, they become disasters when they adversely and seriously affect human life, livelihoods and property. Disaster preparedness, therefore, seeks to prepare for and reduce these adverse effects.

DISASTER MANAGEMENT PLANNING:

Effective Disaster management planning involves identifying organizational resources, determining roles and responsibilities, developing policies and procedures and planning preparedness activities aimed at ensuring timely disaster preparation and effective emergency response.

The actual planning process is preliminary in nature and is performed in a state of uncertainty until an actual emergency or disaster occurs.

TYPES OF DISASTER:

Disasters may represent many different types of events. Disasters may occur suddenly in time (a quick onset), or they may develop over a period of time (a slow onset). Most occur suddenly and perhaps unexpectedly. However, some events develop gradually, including some floods and famines related to drought.

The most widely recognized types of disasters are those listed here -

  • Disasters related to extreme weather events (floods, cyclones, tornadoes, blizzards)
  • Events related to extremes of the earth’s geology (earthquakes, volcanic eruptions). Tsunamis Disasters are commonly categorized by their origin -
  • Natural (including Epidemics)
  • Man-made (including Accidents / Warfare)

Disasters can also be categorized based on their site of origin into:

  • Internal
  • External

INTERNAL DISASTER:

  • Fire/smoke
  • Spillage of Hazardous materials
  • Loss of environmental supplies
  • Leakage of medical gases
  • Explosions
  • Violence Police Action
  • Building collapse

EXTERNAL DISASTER:

  • Natural Hazards (Earthquake, Flood, lightning etc)
  • Civil Disturbance
  • Terrorism
  • Accidents
  • Biological Agents
  • Radiation fallout

DISASTER MANAGEMENT PLAN:

KMH has a disaster management team, according to the type of disaster, which is as follows:

1. CODE BLUE is a code created for the purpose of urgently calling a team of specialists to a particular place to give advanced cardiopulmonary resuscitation in an individual who has experienced cardiopulmonary arrest.

CODE BLUE: Inform to reception

CODE BLUE (CARDIAC ARREST) TEAM:

Code blue team is available 24 hours a day. Code Blue team has been called by anyone from anywhere to provide advanced cardiac life support/pediatric support whenever it is required.

Code Blue Team comprises of: 

  • Medical Officers on Duty
  • Nursing Staff on duty

Telephone operator for immediate contact with code blue team members.

Procedure -

  • One person Leader (DOCTOR) – commend the procedural step
  • Chest compression
  • Ventilation
  • IV access and give medication
  • Keep ready the defibrillator and deliver if required.
  • Document the whole procedure in CPR reporting form.

WHAT DO WE DO?

  • Call nearest medical staff for immediate medical help.
  • Call reception to activate CODE BLUE.
  • Inform CODE BLUE and the Floor, Wing and Bed No.
  • Name of caller informing Code Blue
  • Code Blue Team arrival with crash trolley

ARRANGEMENTS FOR PROVIDING RESUSCITATION EFFORTS:

1. Crash cart with all necessary lifesaving drugs and equipment’s is available ground floor, on first floor in Operation Theatre and in ICU and accessible to all patient areas. Crash cart is kept sealed and used only during medical emergencies.

2. Code blue team to uniformly provide resuscitation in all patient areas. The team members are certified in advanced cardiac life support and basic life support.

3. Training on basic life support to all nursing and medical staff (once in every 3 months)

PROCEDURE:

CODE BLUE TEAM & RESPONSIBILITIES

The code blue cardiopulmonary resuscitation team consists of qualified and trained individuals. Each member of the team has been trained for duties during resuscitation effort.

All code blue team members will be trained in EMS and CPR Training.

PROCEDURE STEP 1:

First check the responsiveness by speaking loudly to the distressed patient, and trying to rouse them by shaking his shoulder.

If there is no response call to activate code blue.

PROCEDURE STEP 2:

If patient is unresponsive, meaning, he is not breathing or his heart has stopped beating, or both, in which case nearest medical / nursing personnel shall be summoned immediately.

PROCEDURE STEP 3:

Reception Person will announce code blue on internal hospital communication system 3 times and send message to the code blue team members through phone.

PROCEDURE STEP 4 :

Initiate basic life support

PROCEDURE STEP 5:

Code blue team has to use lift /stairs to reach the unit, whichever is faster. Code blue team shall keep a target of reaching the site within 3 minutes.

PROCEDURE STEP 6:

Provide resuscitation to the patient as per the training imparted.

Fill the code blue report form after provision of resuscitation effort.

PROCEDURE STEP 7:

Inform patient’s family, if the patient expires, document the events leading to the patient’s death, cause of death, date and time of death.

RESPONSIBILITY: Primary Consultant, ICU Consultant.

CODE BLUE DRILLS

Code blue drills shall be conducted once in 6 months and record shall be maintained. The drill shall be reviewed by Higher Management & Nursing Superintendent to analyze the efficacy of drill

RESPONSIBILITY: Code Blue Coordinator

RESPONSIBILITIES TO ENSURE PROPER CODE BLUE RESPONSE:

Only Code Blue team members are allowed to access open the crash cart.

Once crash cart is opened, it shall recheck and resealed.

All the medicines/ consumable during the code blue call shall be refilled in the crash cart before sealing.

In case there is no code blue call on respective floor for 3 months then crash cart medicines will be checked for quantity and expiry and replaced.

Record is maintained of all expired medicines in the crash cart and forwarded to the pharmacy department

RESPONSIBILITY:

Nurse In charge

REPEAT 5 TIMES

CODE GREEN inform to reception (Natural/External disaster)

External Disaster like accidents with mass casualty, natural disaster like earthquake, flood, severe storm etc, epidemics, bomb blasts or other terrorist activities

There is affixed roster for everyday comprising of on duty staffs from different departments. This team would be led by a staff from the managerial rank, designated as fire protection team leader.

RESPONSIBILITIES OF DISASTER MANAGEMENT TEAM MEMBERS:

MD

  • To mobilize doctors for rendering emergency treatment & triage.
  • To co-ordinate with other health care facilities to organize patient transfer.
  • To collate medical information for patient party / visitor.

NURSING Staff / INCHARGE

  • Identify nursing’s needs
  • Allocating extra nursing staffs in essential areas
  • Re-deploying existing staff and recalling of staff
  • Know current empty beds and number of personnel available whocould assist in other units
  • Send for extra supplies needed from purchasing ,csr ,laundry , and dietary ,drugs , oxygen cylinder etc.
  • Periodic review of arrangements
  • Thereafter and keep all the ots ready to take the patients for surgeries
  • Ensure that additional nurses are available for next shifts

SECURITY:

  • Cordon the area affected / required
  • Regulate entry and exist of personnel to ensure smoot functioning of emergency services
  • Ensure ambulance and other emergency services vehicles
  • Unwanted traffic and public gathering shall be controlled
  • To handle crowd control properly if necessary with police
  • The preservation of specimens and clothing’s that may be needed as evidence of patient will be done by housekeeping and security and due records maintained.
  • Parking arrangements for doctor, relatives of patient to be done outside hospital.
  • Body should be sent to mortuary with proper documentation.
  • To vacant triage & priority 3 areas

ASSEMBLY POINT:

First Point of Contact:

For each type of disaster the person to be contacted first have been identified -

  • CODE RED – inform to reception
  • CODE BLUE inform to reception
  • CODE PINK - inform to reception
  • CODE BLACK inform to reception

AUTHORITIES INVOLVED IN VARIOUS DISASTER SITUATIONS:

For all types of disasters, the “witness” shall intimate the telephone operator, who in turn will be responsible for intimating the first point of contact and informing all relevant people.

ACTIVATION OF CODE RED:

Refer to safety manual

ACTIVATION OF CODE BLUE:

Refer to policy & procedure of uniform use of resuscitation

STEPS TO BE TAKEN IN A DISASTER SITUATION:

  • A Command centre will be set up at the security desk to handle and co-ordinate all internal communication. All departmental heads and designated personnel will report to this office.
  • The Operation Manager will allocate an operator to respond to all the calls received
  • and disseminate necessary information down the line or to the relevant persons.
  • At least one messenger will be assigned to deliver and collect information from the “Emergency Centre”.
  • Nursing Head/ Concerned departmental Head will be notified regarding the type of disaster, number of victims & extent of injuries.
  • Departmental heads will in turn notify their key personnel.
    • A “Control center” for visitors will be set up in the front lobby. Families of the victims can be intimated about the necessary information from this center. A PR representative shall be present at this control center to respond to the queries of the family members of the victims.
    • A list of visitors’ names with details also mentioning the name of the patient they come to inquire about/ visit is maintained.
    • One telephone line will be dedicatedly assigned to the External command center to reciprocate to all relevant queries. A staff shall be assigned for the same.

SUPPLIES & EQUIPMENT:

  • Extra supplies to meet demands shall be procured through runners from the purchase personnel.
    • The Purchase personnel shall organize smooth flow of external supplies of medicines, equipment etc.

VALUABLES & CLOTHING:

Large plastic bags available in the hospital are used for packing patients valuables & clothing, labeled for identification & stored in security room for future retrieval.

MEDICAL RECORDS MAINTENANCE:

A brief clinical note and demographic data shall be maintained for all patients.

HOSPITAL EVACUATION PLAN:

    • In the event of any internal disaster all patients, patient party and personnel shall be removed from the immediate danger area to a safer position in the building / evacuated.
    • Moving will be done in a systematic fashion by moving all patients and personnel closest to the danger first to a safer zone.
    • All ambulatory patients, staff, patient party shall be guided towards the assembly point by the security personnel on duty.
    • Action plan to be announced by On Duty Nursing head in co-ordination with

Medical administration in case of bedridden patients

TRIAGE:

Simple triage is usually used in a scene of a mass-casualty incident (MCI), in order to sort patients into those who need critical attention and immediate transport to the hospital and those with less serious injuries. This step can be started before transportation becomes available. The categorization of patients based on the severity of their injuries

Triage separates the injured into four groups:

  • The deceased
  • The injured who can be helped by immediate transportation
  • The injured whose transport can be delayed
  • Those with minor injuries, who need help less urgently

Use of triage helps designate priorities for treatment further care is based on:

    • Condition & accessibility
    • Availability of time, personnel,
    • Supplies.

DO’S AND DON’T S DURING A DISASTER:

    • Do not panic, Keep yourself cool and calm.

2) Start evacuating the Patients and Personnel from the immediate danger area in a systematic manner.

    • Do not use the elevator.
    • Assemble at the Parking lot which is the assembly point.
